section: third_temple = Ketz HaYamin / explicit Third Temple statements; historical = Mishkan, First or Second Temple as context; comparison = author contrasting them. Gaps are ranked from third_temple rows only

rows.claim: Third Temple has no upper storey; house height 100 amot; author's interior height 85 amot after removing Middos' upper-storey allowance (kiyur 1, dlifah 2, ceiling 1, ma'azivah 1, ma'akeh 3, kalah orev 1) - 'only an opinion'
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 170; Middos 4:6

rows.topic: West window of the Kodesh HaKodashim
rows.claim: Possibly a small window (lul) in the west wall of the Kodesh HaKodashim at 6-8 amot height, as in the Second Temple, to validate slaughter behind the House
rows.source: Zevachim 55b; Gittin 54b Rashi; Middos 4:5

rows.claim: This volume (Part I) covers Yechezkel 40-42 only; chapters 43-48 are cited in passing: city of Yerushalayim south of the Mount, on the slope (45:1-5, 48:10-21); kohanim and Levites dwell around Har HaBayis (45:1-9, p.326); twelve city gates for the twelve tribes (48:30-35, p.224); water flows from the KhK out through the south inner gate (47:1-2, p.340); festival N->S passage and east inner gate opening only Shabbos/Rosh Chodesh (46:1, 9, pp.137, 341); corner kitchens and priestly kitchen (46:19-24, pp.143, 276); altar details deferred to 'Perek 43 note 19' (Part 2)
rows.source: Yechezkel 45-48 as cited by the author
rows.status: cross-references only; not treated in this volume
affects: city massing (city south of the Mount)

rows.claim: Future mountain very high; Yerushalayim on the southern slope; Har HaBayis on the north at the top, 3000 x 3000 amot (1500 x 1500 m); the Beis HaMikdash in the highest place, near the NW of Har HaBayis
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:2 + Rashi; Yeshayahu 2:2; Zecharyah 14:4; Mishkenei Elyon 184, 189; Yechezkel 42:16-20, 45:1-5, 48:10-21

rows.claim: First and Second Temples sat 23 amot below the summit (Ein Eitam 23 amot above the Azarah floor); in the future the site is raised; Har HaZeisim splits N/S and the valley between it and Yerushalayim is filled
rows.source: Zevachim 54b; Yoma 31a; Zecharyah 14:4 + Rashi; Yechezkel 38:20

rows.claim: Even HaShtiya = centre of the world, in the Kodesh HaKodashim; Temple heights: First 120 amot, Second 100, Third 100 (Keser)
rows.source: Chasam Sofer YD 234; Zohar Vayeishev 186; Mishkenei Elyon 150, 170-171; Chaggai 2:9

rows.claim: Diagram B2: Har HaBayis 3000 amot square; open space largest south, then east, then north, least west (labels ~2153 amot south, ~2149 east, 501/500 west/north bands)
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 196 ch.1 m.1; Middos 2:1 pattern

rows.claim: Measuring reed = 6 amot, each amah 6 tefachim (36 tefachim); regular amah 5 tefachim; the angel (Gavriel per Zohar) stands at the gate with linen cord and reed
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:3-5; Targum; Metzudas Dovid; Radak; Zohar Pekudei 233a

rows.claim: Each Har HaBayis gate opening 50 amot high x 10 amot wide (25 m x 5 m), thickness 6 amot = wall; gates have doors; author suggests wall above the opening 10 amot and jamb walls 10 amot, total gate height 60 amot like the eilim
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 170, 172, 196; Sanhedrin 100a / Bava Basra 75a (gates of Yerushalayim 10x20 stones)

rows.claim: Wall of Har HaBayis 6 amot thick x 6 amot high (300 x 300 cm) on all four sides; 3000 x 3000 amot; five gates (2 south, 1 east, 1 north, 1 west)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:5 + Rashi (citing Middos 2:4); Mishkenei Elyon 196 ch.1 m.1-2; Middos 1:3
rows.status: certain for 6x6 and 3000; gates = Mishkenei Elyon/Middos completion

rows.claim: All who enter Har HaBayis enter by the right and circle to exit by the left (e.g. enter east gate, walk north then west, exit south gate); mourners/excommunicated circle left
rows.source: Middos 2:2; Bartenura

rows.topic: Approach to outer court: soreg and cheil
rows.claim: Har HaBayis slopes up toward the west from E/S/N; highest point at the Kodesh HaKodashim. Before the outer court: soreg 10 tefachim high (lattice of wood), then the Cheil = a wall 10 amot high (author draws it 1 amah thick, 'for study'), then 10 amot of open space also called Cheil, then 12 steps (each 0.5 amah rise x 0.5 amah tread; last step 4.5 amot deep) rising 6 amot over 10 amot to the outer east gate
rows.source: Middos 2:3; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 5:3, 6:1; Meiri Middos 2:3 / Yoma 16b; Mishkenei Elyon 191-192, 196 m.3; Rashi 40:6
rows.status: soreg/cheil/12 steps = Middos completion adopted by book; cheil-as-wall = Rambam/Meiri/Mishkenei Elyon (vs Bartenura/TYT soreg-is-cheil-wall); 1 amah thickness = author
affects: east gate stairs (scene has 12 gateway stairs)

rows.claim: Outer court wall 6 amot thick; gate jambs (sippim) 6 amot covering the wall thickness; gate opening 50 amot high, 10 amot wide; the gate has doors (all openings had doors except the Ulam of the House, Middos 2:3)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:6-7; Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 170; Middos 2:3

rows.claim: Gates of outer and inner courts are only 10 amot wide; animals for offering are brought through them (miraculous crowding noted)
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 152; Chazal on standing crowded

rows.claim: Six low cells outside each outer gate on the Har HaBayis side, 3 N and 3 S; each interior 6 x 6 amot (300 cm); walls 5 amot (250 cm) between and on outside; cells project 11 amot (5 wall + 6 cell) toward Har HaBayis; the outer-gate Ulam projects 10 amot into the outer court (8 amot walls + 2 amot eilim); Ulam jambs 6 amot = wall thickness; Ulam gate has doors
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:7-9 + Rashi; Targum; Middos 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon 197 m.5, 199 m.2; Levushei Serad

rows.claim: Cell ceiling thickness not given; author draws 5 amot ceiling and 6 amot interior height so the cell block is 11 amot high; cell floors at the level of the gate floor (top of the 12 steps), entered from the sides of the gate
rows.source: author (*), Mishkenei Elyon 174

rows.claim: Ulam walls 6 amot thick (N-S), 8 amot long projecting west into the outer court; two eilim (round hewn-stone pillars) 2 x 2 amot at the end of the walls, one each side, serving as jambs; doors of the Ulam gate sit between the eilim; total projection 10 amot; Ulam of the outer gate stands exactly opposite the Ulam of the inner gate ('ulam opposite ulam', for beauty)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:8-9 + Rashi; Targum; Mishkenei Elyon 185

rows.claim: Three possibilities for how the Ulam doors open: inward into the Ulam; outward 90 deg to the west into the outer court (author prefers; inner-court north gate tables need room); or 180 deg flat against the 6 amot wall
rows.source: author (*), Rashi 40:9, 40:39

rows.claim: Gate opening width 10 amot everywhere (Har HaBayis gates, court gates, Heikhal) except Kodesh HaKodashim (7) and House Ulam (14); Ulam interior 13 amot N-S (10 + 1.5 + 1.5) by 8 amot E-W; six cells + 4 walls = 38 amot along the wall
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:10-11 + Rashi; Middos

rows.claim: Cell walls begin 2.5 amot from the gate opening on each side (1.5 Ulam offset + 1 amah border); Ulam wall (6) and cell wall (5) end on the same line 7.5 amot from the opening
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:12 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 185

rows.claim: Roof of N cell wall to roof of S cell wall = 25 amot (5+2.5+10+2.5+5), matching Ulam 13 + 6 + 6; cell openings face each other across the gate passage; entrance to cells only from the gate passage, chain-wise 1->2->3
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:13 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 173

rows.claim: Author: the 5 amot cell walls flanking the gate passage rise to the full 50 amot gate height and a ceiling spans the 25 amot passage between the cells (so entering between the cells looks like entering the gate); possibly with a 6 x 5 amot opening in the top 6 amot of each flanking wall (Mishkenei Elyon's 'lights spreading above the cells')
rows.source: author (*); Metzudas Dovid; Binyan HaBayis; Mishkenei Elyon 172, 174
rows.status: author's suggestion; Metzudas Dovid supports a roof

rows.claim: Two round hewn-stone pillars 2 x 2 amot at the west end of each gate Ulam, attached to the wall, 60 amot high (30 m); palm-tree capital possibly 10 amot of the 60 (opening 50 + palm 10); same at N and S outer gates
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:14 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 166, 172, 197 m.4

rows.claim: On the three festivals people enter by the north gate and leave by the south (or vice versa) - court used as a N-S passage; east inner gate opens only Shabbos and Rosh Chodesh (Yechezkel 46); non-Jews bow from Har HaBayis through the gate of entry
rows.source: Yechezkel 46:1, 46:9; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 7:2, 7:16; Keilim 1:8
affects: east inner gate doors normally closed

rows.claim: Outer east gate = 'gate of entry' used all year except the 3 festivals; all gate openings 50 amot high, Ulam openings 50 amot; ceiling thickness unspecified, author suggests 10 amot so gates total 60 amot; author also suggests court walls 60 amot high
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:15 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 170, 172; Sanhedrin 91a/Bava Basra 75a

rows.claim: Windows narrow inside and widening outward (megaphone shape), open (no glass), facing east/outward to Har HaBayis: in the six cells (author draws 12 per gate side), in the jambs of the cell doors (2 per door), in the gate Ulamim (author: 4 per Ulam), and in the outer court wall above the cells (author draws 12 per side E/N/S, none in the corner courts)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:16 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 169; Rabbeinu Bachya Beha'aloscha 8

rows.claim: At the top of each eil a crown (kotheret) shaped like a palm tree (timorah)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:16 + Rashi; Targum

rows.claim: Outer court has 30 chambers on an upper gallery on pillars (gezuztra) whose floor is at 50 amot (gate height), attached to the inside of the outer court wall: 10 east, 10 south, 10 north, none west; author suggests each chamber 10 long x 10 high x 5 wide amot with a 5 amot floor slab so the top reaches 60 amot; gallery length 100 amot per side; possibly for women to watch Simchas Beis HaShoevah
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:17-18 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 185, 197 m.7; Radak; Middos 2:5
rows.status: 30 chambers at 50 amot certain; dimensions author (*)

rows.topic: Gallery interrupted by gates; corner courts
rows.claim: The three gates break the gallery so there are 5 chambers each side of every gate; in the four corners of the outer court are four unroofed small courts 40 x 30 amot for cooking kodashim kalim, with no pillars, gallery or chambers above them; no gallery/chambers on the west
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:18, 46:21-22 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 185, 197 m.7; R' Shemayah (Tzuras HaBayis)

rows.claim: From the outer east gate to the inner east gate = 100 amot (50 m); same in the north (and south, 40:27); all the 100s are 'Keser' perfection
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:19, 23, 27 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 171, 182

rows.claim: North and south outer gates identical to the east gate (50 high x 25 wide, 6 cells, eilim 60 amot with palms, Ulam, narrow windows) EXCEPT seven steps (not twelve): 7 x 0.5 amah rise = 3.5 amot, six treads of 0.5 = 3 amot plus a last step 7 amot deep, starting 10 amot from the Cheil wall; two-leaf doors on the gate; the Ulam has jambs and two doors
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:20-27 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 197
rows.status: certain (7 steps); tread detail = author's summary

rows.claim: Inner court gates have the same measures as the outer gates (opening 10, walls/jambs 6, cells, eilim, windows) except: eight steps, no wall windows (only in the six Ulamim in the wall), and the Ulam and cells are placed differently (Ulam projects OUT into the outer court, cells behind it)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:28-31 + Rashi

rows.topic: Six Ulamim in the inner court wall
rows.claim: Six recesses (Ulamim/porches) built into the thickness of the inner court wall, one each side of each of the 3 inner gates: 25 amot long x 5 amot wide (1250 x 250 cm), leaving 0.5 amah of wall on each face (wall is 6); they have jambs (entrance door in their length, not open along the whole length), narrow windows facing the outer court above the cells (author draws 6 per Ulam), and square reinforcing pillars (atikim) rising ~2/3 of the wall; height not given, author suggests 25 amot
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:29-30, 41:15-16 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 188; Tosafos on 42:3
rows.status: 25x5 in-wall = certain (Rashi); count 6 = author's reasoning; 25 high = author (*)
affects: inner court wall recesses (scene: 'Song chamber' etc.?)

rows.claim: Order of entry to the inner court: eilim (2x2 amot, 60 high, palm capitals) -> Ulam doors 50 amot high between the eilim -> Ulam (walls 8 long x 6 thick; interior 13 N-S x 8 E-W; 50 amot high with a ceiling, author suggests 10 amot thick) -> eight steps rising 4 amot over the 11 amot depth of the cells (7 x 0.5 treads + last step 7.5 amot deep, level with the gate floor) -> gate opening; cells entered from the sides of the gate opening at the top step
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:31 + Rashi; Middos 2:3; Mishkenei Elyon 193
rows.status: certain (8 steps, layout); tread detail author

rows.claim: Inner east gate identical to the inner south gate; author argues a continuous ceiling: Ulam ceiling, ceiling over the 25-amot cell passage, gate ceiling
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:32-34; author (*)

rows.claim: In the inner court, at the WEST shoulder of the north inner gate, a closed chamber (rinsing chamber = slaughterhouse) whose door faces north toward the gate (at the side of the gate, not opposite it); used to rinse innards and stomach and wash meat, and for flaying (hooks) - Third Temple combines what were two places in the Second Temple
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:38 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 177-178, 199 m.3, 202 m.5; Binyan HaAsid (R' Moshe Oyer diagram)
rows.status: certain (existence, north gate); west side = Rashi/Mishkenei Elyon reading

rows.topic: Slaughter tables in the north Ulam
rows.claim: In the Ulam of the inner north gate, two tables on the east and two on the west for slaughtering kodshei kodashim (olah, chatas, asham); the Ulam, though in the outer court, has inner-court sanctity; author suggests the other inner Ulamim may be sanctified too
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:39 + Rashi; Zevachim 47a-48a; Rambam Maaseh HaKorbanos 5:2-3

rows.claim: Above the 8 steps, in the passage between the cells at the level of the gate floor, four more tables: one E and one W of the gate opening, one E and one W beside the Ulam end (i.e. 2 per shoulder); Mishkenei Elyon: 4 tables below in the Ulam and 4 'above at the shoulders of the gate'
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:40 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 177, 202 m.2
rows.status: certain (8 tables total); exact placement per Rashi as read by author

rows.claim: All steps 0.5 amah rise x 0.5 amah tread; 24 cm (Grach Naeh) or ~30 cm (Chazon Ish) per half-amah
rows.source: Middos 2:3
affects: all stairs (scene uses 25 cm at 50 cm/amah)

rows.claim: Standing in the north gate facing north: four tables to the east (2 between cells + 2 in Ulam) and four to the west; all for kodshei kodashim slaughter
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:41

rows.topic: Items not mentioned by the navi
rows.claim: Things certainly present though unmentioned: Aron HaBris and keruvim in the KhK, Menorah, kiyor and its base, golden altar; slaughter of kodshei kodashim also remains in the north of the inner court (the tables are additional)
rows.source: Rashi; Radak; Tosafos Yom Tov; Mishkenei Elyon 177

rows.claim: Second Temple: from N wall 8 amot to Beis HaMitbachayim (12.5 amot, 8 cedar pillars with hooks), tables 8 amot, 24 rings 24 amot; north of the altar
rows.source: Rambam Beis HaBechirah 5:13-14; Middos 3:5, 5:2; Tamid 3:5
affects: none directly; the Third Temple keeps slaughter of kodshei kodashim in the north of the inner court

rows.claim: In the rinsing chamber/slaughterhouse: four marble (hewn stone) tables 1.5 x 1.5 amot, 1 amah high (75 x 75 x 50 cm) for knives and blood-basins, laying the carcass while flaying, rinsing innards and meat; eight low cedar pillars (nanasim) with iron hooks 1 tefach (8 cm) in 3 rows (or 3 directions) for hanging and flaying; hooks possibly also in the walls; author: more than 8 pillars at festivals, and possibly a second open-air flaying area in the Azarah
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:42-43 + Rashi; Targum; Pesachim 65a; Tamid 3:5, 4:2; Middos 3:5; Mishkenei Elyon 177-178, 199
rows.status: tables certain; 8 pillars = Second Temple pattern adopted; extras = author (*)
affects: kitchens/slaughter chamber props (scene has 8 'Stone slaughter table' + 'Knife-store niches' + hooks?)

rows.claim: A third inner-court chamber at the NORTH shoulder of the inner east gate, door facing north, for the Kohanim bnei Tzadok (charge of the altar) - where they don their white linen garments; called the Chamber of Clothing (Lishkas HaLevush)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:46; Mishkenei Elyon 179, 199 m.3

rows.claim: Inner court: a chamber for the Levite singers at the EAST shoulder of the north inner gate (between the north gate and the east wall), one from outside but divided into two inside, doors facing south; holds lyres, harps, cymbals and all instruments
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:44-45 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 178-179, 199 m.3; Binyan HaAsid / R' Moshe Oyer
rows.status: certain (existence, north gate, faces south); east side per Rashi/Mishkenei Elyon

rows.claim: Second Temple: 96 sealed windows/niches for the four garments of the ordinary kohanim, 4 per mishmar (pants, sashes, hats, tunics), names written on them (diagram of the garment chamber with 24 mishmaros)
rows.source: Rambam Klei HaMikdash 8:8-9
rows.status: historical, author draws it into the Third-Temple garment chamber

rows.claim: Inner court 100 x 100 amot square; the altar in its exact centre, 34 amot from the Ulam; E-W: Yisroel 17 + Kohanim 17 + altar 32 + 34 to the Ulam = 100; N-S: 4 amot wall to ramp, ramp + altar 62, remainder 34 to the north wall; altar 32 x 32 amot; the Tapuach (ash heap) on the altar centre is in line with the Even HaShtiya and the golden altar; kiyor and its base and the ash place (beis hadeshen) must also be present
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:47 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 182, 198 m.1, 204 m.2; Tosafos Yom Tov Tzuras HaBayis
rows.status: certain (100x100, altar before the House); 34/17/17 split = Mishkenei Elyon (vs 22 in the Second Temple)

rows.claim: Between Ezras Yisroel and Ezras Kohanim: a step 1 amah high with the duchan on it having three steps of 0.5 amah, so Ezras Kohanim is 2.5 amot above Ezras Yisroel (per R' Eliezer b. Yaakov); adopted for the Third Temple diagram
rows.source: Middos 2:6; see also 42:12 discussion

rows.claim: Inner court has three gates (E, N, S); the House (100 amot wide) closes its whole west side; court wall 6 amot thick and (by reasoning) 60 amot high
rows.source: Yechezkel 40-41; author's reasoning

rows.topic: Shift of the House relative to the altar
rows.claim: Altar position is fixed forever (Rambam), so the House moves: 34 instead of 22 amot from the altar (+12) and the KhK wall is 2 amot instead of 1 amah traksin (+1): the Kodesh HaKodashim is 13 amot further west than in the Second Temple; Even HaShtiya (per Zohar) fills the whole KhK so the Aron still rests on it
rows.source: Rambam Beis HaBechirah 2:1, 2:3; Middos 4:7, 5:1; Zohar

rows.claim: To add in the inner court: (1) kiyor and base between the Ulam and the altar (d'Oraisa) with its pit and pulley (muchni) to lower it at night; (2) ash place (beis hadeshen) east of the altar, 10 amot north of the ramp start and 3 tefachim east; (3) the drain opening (shis) at the SW corner of the altar; (4) two tables west of the ramp - one for the 93 service vessels, one for the fats; (5) fire-pan / blood drains at the SW corner; two cups for wine and water libation
rows.source: Torah; Middos 3:6, 5:?; Tamid; Rambam; book's own 'Perek 43 note 19' (Part 2)
rows.status: d'Oraisa items certain; positions from Middos (Second Temple) adopted

rows.claim: Flanking the Ulam on N and S: Beis HaChalifos 15 amot long each (5 amot outer wall + 10 amot hollow N-S), only 10 amot deep E-W (Rashi 41:12), its 5-amot east wall part of the 100-amot facade; author draws its west wall 1 amah leaving 4 amot of passage/knife storage; between Ulam and Beis HaChalifos an unnamed space; possibly (author) two small side chambers 8 amot high as in the Second Temple, and pishpashim (small doors) in the NW/SW corners
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:48, 41:12 + Rashi; Middos 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon 176, 202 ch.3 m.1; Zevachim 55b
affects: Ulam wings (scene 'Knife-store wing' x2, 'Knife-store niches' x18)

rows.claim: Ulam entrance wall 5 amot thick (E-W) each side; jambs project 3 amot into the opening from N and S so the OPENING IS 14 AMOT WIDE (700 cm), not 20 as in the Second Temple; opening 50 amot high (Mishkenei Elyon); Ulam interior 20 (N-S) x 11 (E-W); Ulam walls 5 amot E/N/S; facade wall 100 amot long
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:48 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 170, 202 ch.3 m.1
rows.status: certain (14 wide is explicit in Rashi's reading); 50 high = Mishkenei Elyon
affects: Ulam facade opening (scene 'Ulam nested stone door frame')

rows.topic: Ulam and its steps and pillars
rows.claim: Ulam 20 (N-S) x 11 (E-W) amot; approached by TWELVE steps 0.5 amah high (6 amot total), arranged per Middos 3:6 as amah, amah, 3-amah landing (x3) then amah, amah, 4-amah landing = 21 amot long; two pillars (eilim) 2 x 2 amot, 60 amot high with palm capitals flank the entrance 'in place of Yachin and Boaz' (which were 36 x 4 amot)
rows.source: Yechezkel 40:49 + Rashi; Middos 3:6; Rambam 6:4; Melachim I 7:16; Mishkenei Elyon 166, 172, 197
rows.status: 12 steps = Rashi via Middos; 60-amah pillars = Mishkenei Elyon parallel

rows.claim: Whether pishpashim (small side doors at 8 amot height in Beis HaChalifos and behind the Heichal) exist in the Third Temple is not said by Rashi/Mishkenei Elyon; author: possibly, to permit kodashim kalim slaughter there
rows.source: Zevachim 55b-56a; Rambam 6:8

rows.claim: Diagram: Ulam (12 steps), Beis HaChalifos with pishpashim, munach, Heichal 40 x 20, KhK 20 x 20 with Even HaShtiya, mesibah (winding stair) and Beis Horadas HaMayim (water descent) at the west, side chambers 5/6/9 amot
rows.source: book diagram

rows.claim: All walls of the Heikhal and KhK are 6 amot (300 cm) thick on all four sides; Heikhal entrance height 50 amot (Mishkenei Elyon)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:1, 5, 12, 13 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 165, 170, 204

rows.claim: Heikhal 40 long x 20 wide amot (2000 x 1000 cm); entrance 10 amot wide (500 cm), 5 amot of wall each side; height of the entrance 50 amot (2500 cm); doorpost square (four-sided frame), two doors right and two left (folding)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:2, 21 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 164, 169, 170, 203 ch.3 m.2

rows.claim: Wall between Kodesh and KhK 2 amot thick (100 cm); entrance 6 amot high x 7 amot wide (300 x 350 cm), square 4-post frame; two doors ALWAYS OPEN (author: open inward, like the Heikhal doors); before the entrance a paroches exactly the size of the gate 'no less and no more' hiding the interior; the Aron's poles press into the paroches
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:3, 21, 23 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 159-160, 166, 203; Yoma 54a; Shemos 26:31-33
rows.status: wall/door dims certain; paroches = Mishkenei Elyon (not in navi); inward = author (*)

rows.claim: First Temple: 1-amah wall (amah traksin) with 5-post doorway and doors + paroches; Second Temple: no wall, two parochos with an amah between (doubt which side the amah belonged to)
rows.source: Rambam 4:2; Yoma 51b; Middos 4:7; Melachim I 6:31

rows.claim: KhK 20 x 20 amot (1000 x 1000 cm), 'closed mem'; contains the Even HaShtiya (raised 3 fingerbreadths, Yoma 53b) with the Aron on it (Luchos, Sefer Torah), poles at its sides, kaporet and keruvim with spread wings, beside it Aharon's staff, anointing-oil flask, manna jar; no upper storey; a window in the west wall (author)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:4; Rambam 4:1; Yoma 53b; Tosafos Yom Tov Yoma 5:2; Tanchuma Kedoshim 10; Mishkenei Elyon 150, 167
rows.status: 20x20 certain; contents = Torah/Rambam completion; Aron position: west (Rambam) vs centre (Tosafos Yom Tov) unresolved

rows.claim: Even HaShtiya may occupy most of the KhK; author's study-only suggestion: 12 x 12 amot (600 x 600 cm) centred, raised 3 fingerbreadths (~6 cm); reconciles Rambam (west), Tosafos Yom Tov (centre) and 'protruding east'
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 150; Rambam 4:1; Yoma 53b

rows.claim: Aron: 2.5 x 1.5 x 1.5 amot (15 x 9 x 9 tefachim wooden box, inner gold box 1 tefach smaller, outer 1 tefach larger), gold crown (zer), 4 rings at the top corners with permanent gold-covered poles; contents Luchos, broken Luchos, Sefer Torah; kaporet gold slab 1 tefach thick; two keruvim hammered from it, wings spread over, faces toward each other and down to the kaporet, child-like faces, body height 10 tefachim (83 cm), 'six wings each' (book's own statement)
rows.source: Shemos 25:10-22; Rashi; Bava Basra 14a-b; Sukkah 5b
rows.status: Torah = certain; six wings = book's statement without source

rows.topic: Items to return in the Third Temple
rows.claim: All five missing in the Second Temple return: Aron with poles, kaporet, keruvim, staff of Aharon, anointing oil, manna jar, Luchos and broken Luchos, Sefer Torah of Moshe; fire, Shechinah, Urim v'Tumim
rows.source: Yoma 21b; Binyan HaBayis (R' Yechiel Hillel) 34; Mishkenei Elyon 167

rows.claim: Roof section following Middos 4:6 applied to the Third Temple: otem (foundation) 6, interior height (author) 85, ceiling 5 (kiyur 1 with gold-coated decorated beams, beis dilfah 2, tikrah 1, maazivah 1), maakeh 3, kalah orev 1 (iron spikes against birds; author keeps it 'not to change from Middos', or 4 amot maakeh per R' Yehudah)
rows.source: Middos 4:6; Meiri; Rambam; Tosafos Moed Katan 9a
rows.status: author's suggestion (roof layers), kalah orev debated
affects: Heikhal roof (scene 'Golden roof anti-bird point' x70)

rows.claim: Western KhK wall 6 amot; behind it one western chamber 4 amot wide x 22 amot long; N and S chambers 11 amot long x 4 amot wide (interior), walls 5 amot; chambers adjoin the House wall directly (Rashi per R' Shemayah; Mishkenei Elyon 204: 'ta 4, wall 5'); eastern chambers have a wall toward the munach
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:5 + Rashi (corrected per R' Shemayah); Mishkenei Elyon 180-181, 204 ch.4 m.4, ch.5 m.1; Tzuras HaBayis; Levushei Serad
rows.status: certain (4 wide, 5 walls); 11 long = Rashi corrected; 22 west = author's inference
affects: side cells around the Heikhal (scene 'cells' 110 arch + 15 'Side-cell floor')

rows.claim: 33 chambers: 15 N, 15 S (5 per storey x 3), 3 W (1 per storey); widths 4 (ground), 5 (middle), 6 (top) as the House wall steps back 1 amah per storey (6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 3); cedar ceiling beams rest on the steps of the House wall and are socketed into holes in the 5-amot outer chamber wall; author: each storey interior 6 high + 5 ceiling = 11, so 33 amot total = 1/3 of the House height, ceilings/floors gold-covered where wood shows
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:6-7 + Rashi; Melachim I 6:6, 6:10; Middos 4:4; Mishkenei Elyon 180-181, 203 ch.4 m.2-3; Bava Basra 61a
rows.status: 33 / widths 4-5-6 / stepped wall / cedar = certain; heights = author (*)

rows.claim: Chambers used for storing gold, silver and precious vessels / weaving curtains / Temple treasuries
rows.source: Tavnis HaBayis; Tiferes Yisroel Middos 1:1; Beis HaMikdash HaShlishi (Steinberg) 196

rows.claim: Ascent between the three storeys of side chambers by a winding stair: a round stone pillar with steps circling it ('shvindel-stein'); author draws it rising only to the 2nd and 3rd floors; the roofs are reached by the separate Mesibah corridor (Middos 4:5) from the NE to the NW corner
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:7 + Rashi; Targum; Melachim I 6:8; Middos 4:3, 4:5; Mishkenei Elyon
rows.status: certain (winding stair exists); placement = author's explanation 2

rows.claim: Foundations of the chamber walls 6 amot wide below ground (the extra amah of foundation projects toward the House on N/S and outward in the west, counting in the 100-amot length); otem height 6 amot as in Middos 4:6 (author); visible above the inner court floor either side of the Ulam steps
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:8 + Rashi; Middos 4:6; Mishkenei Elyon 181, 203

rows.claim: House height 100 amot (5000 cm), also 100 long and 100 wide; the 100-high block spans the 90 x 32 amot Ulam-Heikhal-KhK body AND the full 100-amot east front (including Beis HaChalifos); the side chambers behind are low (author: about 1/3, i.e. 33 amot); no upper storey (vs First Temple 120 with upper storey); House 'like a lion': 100 wide in front, 70 behind
rows.source: Rashi 41:8 (Middos 4:6); Mishkenei Elyon 170-171; Middos 4:7; Rambam 4:9; Yeshayahu 29:1
rows.status: 100 high = certain (book); front-block-100 high & cells 1/3 = author (*)

rows.topic: Munach and access to the chambers
rows.claim: Chamber walls above ground 5 amot; ground-floor chambers at the level of the House floor (not at the otem); 'munach' = open space 5 amot wide in the NE and SE corners (between the chambers and the Ulam), author: 20 amot long (spanning ta 4 + wall 5 + mesibah/water house 5 + wall 5 + 1); the ONLY entrance to the chambers is from the munach (chain-wise, 3 doors each; NE chamber 5 doors incl. one to the Heikhal, possibly a permanently closed one on the SE); the munach is reached from pishpashim (small doors) in the Ulam either side of the Heikhal gate - north pishpash always open, south pishpash always closed (Yechezkel 44:1-2)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:9-11 + Rashi (interpretation A per R' Shemayah); Middos 4:3; Mishkenei Elyon 180, 203-204; Yechezkel 44:1-2
rows.status: munach 5 wide + corner position certain; length 20 = author; pishpash rule = pasuk

rows.topic: Priestly chambers building north of the House
rows.claim: 20 amot north of the House's outer wall (the chamber wall), at the level of the inner court floor, a 3-storey building 100 amot long x 50 amot wide containing chambers (detailed in 42:1-14)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:10 + Rashi

rows.topic: Width 70 behind; Mesibah and Beis Horadas HaMayim
rows.claim: West block 70 amot wide N-S: Heikhal/KhK body 32 (20 + 6 + 6) + 38 of low building = ta 4 + ta wall 5 + Mesibah 5 + its wall 5 (north) and ta 4 + ta wall 5 + Beis Horadas HaMayim (water descent) 5 + its wall 5 (south); chambers 85 long + munach 5 = 90 amot to the Beis HaChalifos; Ulam and its walls 30 wide only
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:12 + Rashi; Middos 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon 181, 204 ch.5 m.1
rows.status: certain (book adopts Mishkenei Elyon's 5/5 split; Middos had 3/5)

rows.topic: Mesibah and roof access; water drainage
rows.claim: Mesibah: a sloping passage from the NE corner along the north to the NW, then along the west to the S, giving access to the roofs of the cells (exit opening 12:3c) and by ladder/cedar posts to the House roof; a 'lul' hatch on the House roof; Beis Horadas HaMayim: the south corridor where roof water drains down (diagram 12:6a-b)
rows.source: Middos 4:5, 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon 181, 204; Tiferes Yisroel
rows.status: Middos completion adopted (Mishkenei Elyon names both)

rows.claim: E-W: Ulam wall 5 + Ulam 11 + Heikhal wall 6 + Heikhal 40 + KhK wall 2 + KhK 20 + west wall 6 + west ta 4 + ta foundation 6 = 100 amot; on the sides: 90 + Beis HaChalifos 10 = 100; cedar beams from the Heikhal wall to the Ulam wall for bracing (Middos 3:8) also in the Third Temple
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:13 + Rashi; Middos 3:8, 4:7

rows.topic: Passage between Ulam and Beis HaChalifos
rows.claim: Between the Ulam and each Beis HaChalifos a 20-amot long, 10-amot wide space: 5 amot east wall + 5 for interior and west wall (author: 4 interior + 1 wall, braced by beams)
rows.source: Tosafos Yom Tov Middos 4:7; author (*)

rows.claim: Front: Ulam 20 (opening 14) + 5-amot east wall running 43 amot N and 43 S = 100; Beis HaChalifos 15 N-S x 10 E-W each (10 hollow + 5 wall); book draws a partition wall with an opening marking the start of the Beis HaChalifos; front is 100 amot HIGH across its whole width (author reads Rashi/Mishkenei Elyon); Beis HaChalifos hold knives - south: knives for repair/genizah, north: knives ready for slaughter, in racks per 24 mishmaros (diagrams 14a/14b)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:14 + Rashi; Middos 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon 176, 204; Binyan HaAsid 539
rows.status: 100 wide certain; 100 high across front = author's reading; knife racks per mishmar = author's diagram

rows.claim: The Heikhal (Gizrah), the Kodesh HaKodashim and the six Ulamim of the inner court wall all have: door jambs (sippim), narrow windows, and 'atikim' = square reinforcing pillars projecting from the wall
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:15-16 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 169, 203 ch.3 m.5

rows.topic: Wall lining: cedar panels overlaid with gold
rows.claim: KhK and Heikhal walls, their door jambs and their doors are overlaid with pure gold from floor to ceiling; since gold cannot be laid on stone, the walls are panelled with thin cedar boards (carved) and the gold beaten into the carving; ceiling carved with designs and gold-covered; only the window openings stay open; Ulam door jambs also gold over carved palms; Ulam walls themselves (book diagram 18) of precious stone, no gold mentioned
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:16-17 + Rashi; Targum; Melachim I 6:32 + Rashi/Radak/Malbim; Tikkunei Zohar 21

rows.claim: Reinforcing square pillars, three per side (N and S) in the KhK and three per side in the Heikhal, projecting both outside and inside the wall, rising about 2/3 of the wall height then tapering (Tosafos); same in the six inner-court Ulamim, whose height is possibly 25 amot
rows.source: Mishkenei Elyon 169; Tosafos on 42:3 (in Rashi)
rows.status: existence certain; count 3 per side = Mishkenei Elyon as read by author

rows.claim: Number/place of the narrow windows not given; author: high on the walls above the side chambers; 12 in the KhK (3 per side incl. 3 east above the door) after the 12 gates/12 tribes and R' Shimon Chirari's shul; Heikhal 4 N, 4 S, 4 E above the gate; each inner-court Ulam 6 windows (12 per side); windows always open, no glass (Rashi's 'sealed from within' is a corrupt gloss)
rows.source: author (*); Yechezkel 48:30-35; R' Chaim Vital Pri Etz Chaim; Mishkenei Elyon 169; Levushei Serad
affects: Heikhal high windows (scene 'High narrow window' x16, 'Splayed high window stone reveal' x72)

rows.claim: Second Temple: two golden crowns (bowls) on two windows in the Heikhal toward the Ulam for beauty - ordinary windows, Second Temple only
rows.source: Middos 3:8; Tosafos Gittin 7a

rows.claim: First Temple: gold sheets beaten into the carved forms so the carving remains visible, fixed with gold nails; in the Devir cast into the carving, in the Heikhal sheets hammered in
rows.source: Melachim I 6:32, 35 + Rashi/Radak/Malbim; Divrei HaYamim II 3:5
rows.status: historical technique the book applies to the Third Temple finish

rows.claim: Cedar-over-stone with gold over the cedar on ALL walls of the KhK and Heikhal, floor to ceiling, above the door, and (unlike the Second Temple) even the wall behind the open doors; ceiling gold with carved designs; author: floor also cedar boards carved with designs and gold-covered as in the First Temple; gold sheets fixed with gold nails; Third Temple of silver, gold and precious stones (Tikkunei Zohar 21)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:17, 20 + Rashi; Middos 4:1; Melachim I 6:21-22, 30; Mishkenei Elyon 168; Tikkunei Zohar 21; Zeved Tov
rows.status: walls/ceiling certain (Rashi); behind doors = author's inference; floor = author (*)
affects: Heikhal/Kodesh wall, ceiling and floor finish

rows.claim: Wall panels carved with alternating keruv, palm, keruv, palm...; each keruv has TWO faces (only faces, not full bodies): young lion's face on the keruv's right turning toward the palm on its right, man's face on its left toward the palm on its left; carved in cedar, gold beaten into the carving so the forms stay legible; lion on the right = Mishkenei Elyon's 'right/chesed'; author speculates six wings per keruv in the future
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:18-19 + Rashi; Targum; Radak; Metzudas Dovid; Malbim; Mishkenei Elyon 168, 190-191, 203 ch.3 m.4; Chagigah 13b; Sukkah 5b
rows.status: certain (two faces, lion+man, palms between); side assignment = Mishkenei Elyon; six wings = author
affects: wall reliefs (scene has palm-only panel; keruv panels never modelled)

rows.claim: Reliefs on all walls of the KhK floor to ceiling, on the door jambs and the doors, above the entrance; likewise on all Heikhal walls floor to ceiling including the wall behind the doors
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:19-20 + Rashi; Melachim I 6:20, 30; Mishkenei Elyon 168

rows.claim: Heikhal entrance has straight (square-cornered, not round or 5-sided) posts: threshold, straight lintel, two jambs; opening 10 wide x 50 high (Mishkenei Elyon; Second Temple was 20 high); in the KhK the prophet saw an appearance like the Throne of Glory
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:21 + Rashi; Targum; Melachim I 6:33; Mishkenei Elyon 169-170; Middos 4:1

rows.claim: Between shulchan and menorah, on the Heikhal centre line opposite the Aron, drawn slightly east of them; all three in the western half of the 40-amah Heikhal (= Rambam's 'third' of the 60-amah House, Menachos 98b, Yerushalmi Shekalim 6:3); 1 x 1 amah x 2 high with the amah of 5 tefachim (~41.7 x 41.7 x 83 cm); acacia overlaid with gold, four horns, incense twice daily
rows.source: Shemos 30:1-10; Rashi Shemos 26:35; Yoma 33b; Menachos 98b; Rambam 3:17; Eruvin 4a on Yechezkel 43:13; Mishkenei Elyon 167, 193

rows.claim: Golden menorah, one hammered kikar, south of the Heikhal opposite the shulchan, 2.5 amot from the south wall, 5 amot from the KhK wall; height 18 tefachim (150 cm at 50 cm/amah); branches N-S (Rambam; Rashi E-W drawn as alternative 22:23a); six wicks toward the middle lamp, middle lamp toward the KhK; a three-step stone before it for the kohen; lit even on Shabbos
rows.source: Shemos 25:31-40, 26:35 + Rashi; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 3:8, 3:10-12; Menachos 98b (R' Elazar b. R' Shimon); Mishkenei Elyon 167, 173
rows.status: position certain; orientation = Rambam adopted; 18 tefachim = Rambam

rows.claim: Shulchan 2 amot long (E-W, 'its length along the length of the House') x 1 wide x 3 HIGH (100 x 50 x 150 cm; Third Temple height differs from Torah's 1.5), wood overlaid with gold, north of the Heikhal, 2.5 amot from the north wall, 5 amot from the KhK wall; 12 loaves always on it (see keilim review for details)
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:22 + Rashi/Targum; Shemos 25:23, 26:35 + Rashi; Yoma 33b; Menachos 98b-99a; Baraisa d'Meleches HaMishkan; Rambam 3:12; Mishkenei Elyon 167, 203
rows.status: certain (book's main line); alternative that 3 amot includes the bread noted p.246

rows.claim: Diagram 22(a): the outer stone altar in the inner court; Torah measures of the altar are not indispensable - may be enlarged (Zevachim 62a), never smaller than Moshe's; the ketores altar in the Heikhal burns incense twice daily
rows.source: Zevachim 62a; Ohr HaChaim Shemos 25:9; Chasam Sofer YD 236; Ramban

rows.claim: Twelve folded loaves in two stacks of six (each loaf 1 tefach thick, folded to 6 x 5 tefachim, laid across the table width), 28 half-tube golden rods (3 per loaf, 2 on the top loaf) on 4 golden upright plates (snifin) 5 tefachim wide reaching 5 amot above the floor; two golden bowls of frankincense between the stacks; the loaves wait in the Ulam on a marble table (north side) before Shabbos and the old ones go to a golden table on the Ulam's south side
rows.source: Menachos 94-99; Rambam Temidin uMusafin 5, Beis HaBechirah 3:12-16; Rashi Shemos 25:29

rows.topic: Doors of the Heikhal and KhK
rows.claim: Heikhal: two doors 50 amot high x 5 wide each closing the 10-amah opening, locked every evening and opened every morning (via the north pishpash -> cell -> Heikhal); KhK: two cedar doors carved with keruvim and palms, gold-overlaid, 6 amot high x 3.5 wide each (300 x 175 cm), ALWAYS open, paroches spread over the opening; Second Temple doors changed to gold when Israel grew rich
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:23 + Rashi; Targum; Mishkenei Elyon 170; Middos 2:3, 4:1-2; Tamid 3:7; Melachim I 6:31-32

rows.claim: Three options: doors open inward into the KhK (author prefers, since the paroches is 'the measure of the gate, no less no more' and the Heikhal doors open inward); or outward with the paroches between; or folded against the wall; paroches of blue, purple, scarlet and linen with keruvim on both sides (Torah); poles of the Aron press into it like 'two breasts'
rows.source: Menachos 98a-b; Mishkenei Elyon 166; Shemos 26:31-33; Yoma 54a; Abarbanel

rows.claim: Heikhal entrance wall 6 amot thick; OUTER pair of doors 5 amot wide each (50 high) set 1 amah in from the jamb, opening inward to lie against the 5-amot wall thickness (the extra amah = door thickness, author suggests doors 1 amah thick); INNER pair at the Heikhal face opening onto the 5-amot 'shoulders' of the Heikhal inside; Rambam/Ramchal follow the Tanna Kamma (Rashi also cites R' Yehudah's folding-door version); western pair opened first each morning, then the eastern
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:24 + Rashi; Middos 4:1; Rambam 4:7; Mishkenei Elyon

rows.claim: All four Heikhal doors carved with keruvim (lion right, man left) and palms, cedar, gold overlaid, like the walls and the KhK doors; thick cedar beams run from the Heikhal wall to the Ulam wall for bracing and PROTRUDE east through the Ulam facade toward the inner court, gold-overlaid; author draws 10 beams 6 amot wide x 2 thick ending at 60 amot height, also along the Ulam sides to the Beis HaChalifos; no exposed wood anywhere in the House or courts
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:25 + Rashi; Middos 3:8; Mishkenei Elyon 171, 202 ch.3 m.4; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 1:9, Avodas Kochavim 6:9-10; Radak; Metzudas Dovid
rows.status: beams protruding = Rashi/Radak certain; 10 x (6x2) = author (*); gold = author

rows.claim: Second Temple: five carved olive-wood beams stepped above the Ulam entrance, each protruding 1 amah further per side; not mentioned for the Third Temple; author speculates the palm-capped eilim take their place / form a canopy
rows.source: Middos 3:7
affects: Ulam facade (scene has 'Layered Ulam roof cornice' x5 and 'Ulam lintel moulding' x6 - Second-Temple-style)

rows.claim: Narrow (splayed) windows on both sides of the Ulam entrance within the 5-amot thick side walls (author: possibly along the whole front to the Beis HaChalifos, possibly 12); palm-tree reliefs only (no keruvim) on the Ulam door jambs, cedar with gold; author: the Ulam may have doors with palms only (Second Temple had a curtain, no doors); ceiling: 'ribs' = horizontal cedar beams (2 amot, beis dilfah) on top of the walls carrying the thick rafters (1 amah tikrah), plus 1 amah kiyur of carved gold designs and 1 amah maazivah = 5 amot ceiling; whole ceiling gold with carved designs and bowls
rows.source: Yechezkel 41:26 + Rashi; Chazal (Middos 4:6); Radak; Metzudas Dovid; Tiferes Yisroel
rows.status: windows/palms certain; Ulam doors and counts = author (*)

rows.claim: In the NW of the outer court (and mirrored in the S) a block of chambers 100 amot long (E-W, parallel to the House) x 50 wide, 3 storeys, separated 20 amot from the House's outer (mesibah) wall; floor at the inner-court level; entered only from the outer court (the House's 100-amot front seals the inner court's west); the chambers count as inner court (kodshei kodashim eaten there)
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:1-2 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 186-187, 198 ch.1 m.8-9; Menachos 96a
affects: priest chambers block N and S (scene 'priest' 218 arch, 30 floors/roofs)

rows.topic: Open space north of the chambers
rows.claim: From the chambers' north doors to the outer court's north wall 50 amot of open space, 100 amot long; chamber doors face north (also doors south into the 20-amot strip)
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:2, 4 + Rashi; 46:19

rows.topic: The 20-amot strip and the priestly kitchen
rows.claim: The 20-amot strip between the House's side building and the chambers belongs to the inner court (Menachos 96a); its WEST end on the NORTH side is the place where kohanim cook the chatas/asham and bake menachos (kodshei kodashim) - ovens; kodashim kalim are cooked in the four corner courts of the outer court instead; south strip does not cook
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:3, 46:19-20 + Rashi; Menachos 96a; Rambam Maaseh HaKorbanos 11:21-22; Mishkenei Elyon 187, 198

rows.topic: Access between inner court and the 20-amot strip
rows.claim: How kodshei kodashim reach the strip: author prefers an opening (one amah) in the inner court's N/S wall into the strip, reading Rashi 'outer OR inner'; alternatives: via Ulam -> pishpash -> munach, or a sanctified tunnel; transfer north->south chambers via the west (KhK lul) or via the Ulam and Beis HaChalifos pishpash
rows.source: Rashi 42:1, 4 (text variants); Levushei Serad; Sachaf Etz; Zevachim 55b

rows.claim: Entry from the outer court into the 20-amot strip is through a sloped opening only 1 amah wide (author: possibly 2 amot long) cut at the end of the 6-amot wall dividing the courts, into a 5-amot wide x 10-amot long passage between the Beis HaChalifos and the chambers, then into the 20-amot strip; the '20' = 15 behind the Beis HaChalifos + 5 of the wall; extra amah = author's 1-amah atik pillar projection
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:4 + Rashi (per R' Shemayah); Mishkenei Elyon 198 ch.1 m.9; Sukkah 7b
rows.status: certain (1-amah way, Rashi); atik amah = author
affects: inner/outer court wall at the NW/SW corners

rows.claim: Three storeys; third storey narrower INSIDE because the 'atikim' (thick supports) fill its N and S walls and eat into its space; from them three pillars descend through the 2nd and 1st storeys inside the wall thickness, projecting ~1 amah in and out, down to the foundations; built from the top down (Mishkenei Elyon), no external buttresses needed; author's 'by way of example' numbers: block 100 x 50 x ~50 high, storeys ~10 amot clear, walls/ceilings ~5 amot, 3rd-storey N/S atik walls ~10 thick x 10 high, 3rd-storey interior ~30 x 90, lower storeys ~40 x 90, pillars ~7 amot thick, rectangular; Tosafos/Metzudas Dovid read the opposite (atikim below)
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:3-6 + Rashi/Tosafos; Radak; Mishkenei Elyon 186-187, 198 ch.1 m.8
rows.status: layout = Rashi + Mishkenei Elyon; all numbers = author (D.M. 'for example')

rows.claim: The chambers' east wall facing the outer court is 50 amot wide (= chamber width, excluding atik projections) and is a 'fence' guarding the kodshei kodashim area from the crowds passing on the east; chambers 100 long opposite the whole House
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:7-8 + Rashi; Keilim 1:8

rows.topic: Height terraces of the whole complex
rows.claim: Levels (author's synthesis): Even HaShtiya +3 fingers above the House floor; House (Ulam/Heikhal/KhK) highest, 6 amot above the inner court (12 Ulam steps); inner court = Azarah + Ezras Kohanim = upper chambers = 20-amot strip; Ezras Yisroel 2.5 amot lower (duchan: 1 amah step + 3 half-steps); west of the outer court lower by >=2.5 (slope into the strip, author ~3 amot); outer court N/S gate floors 4 amot below the inner court (8 steps), east outer court 6.5 below (8 steps + duchan 2.5); lower (east) chambers at the outer-court level without steps; Har HaBayis 3.5 amot below the outer court at N/S gates (7 steps), 6 amot at the east gate (12 steps); mountain slopes down on all four sides
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:9 + Rashi; Middos 2:3, 2:6; Yoma 16b; Mishkenei Elyon 192-193, 196, 198; author
rows.status: step counts certain; slopes and exact west levels = author (*)

rows.claim: In the NE (and SE) of the outer court, chambers without atikim called 'lower chambers' because they are at the foot of the mountain, entered from the east at outer-court level, no steps
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:9 + Rashi

rows.topic: Access to the upper chambers and behind the House
rows.claim: Northern upper chambers entered from their north side by steps ~3.5 amot; from the 20-amot strip without steps; from the strip's west end down ~8 steps (~4 amot) to the 11-amot space behind the House
rows.source: author (*), Mishkenei Elyon 192-193

rows.claim: Position not settled: Rambam - west of the KhK; Tosafos Yom Tov / Tanchuma - centre (Tanchuma: stone visible 'before the Aron', i.e. protruding east); Mishkenei Elyon - 'in the place of' the KhK; author reconciles by letting the stone spread ~12 x 12 amot from the centre (study only); steps of 6 amot suggested in the munach up to the cells
rows.source: Rambam 4:1; Tosafos Yom Tov Yoma 5:2; Tanchuma Kedoshim 10; Mishkenei Elyon 150, 167; Zohar Noach 70a-b

rows.claim: Five levels: KhK (King alone), Heikhal (souls of Israel, incense altar), inner court incl. upper chambers and 20-amot strip (Serafim, outer altar), outer court incl. lower chambers (Chayos), Har HaBayis 500 x 500 reeds (Ofanim / all creatures); lower chambers 'closer to the court'

rows.topic: Lower chambers (NE and SE of the outer court)
rows.claim: Lower chambers 100 (E-W) x 50 (N-S) amot, 3 storeys, no atikim, adjacent to the north (and south) wall of the inner court, beginning at the east end of the gate cells (sharing the cells' half-amah wall) so that an 11-amot passage remains between their east end and the outer court's east wall (mirroring the 11 amot behind the House in the west); they block the outer court's north/south passage except that 11-amot corridor
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:9-10 + Rashi; Mishkenei Elyon 184-187, 197 ch.1 m.7; Tzuras HaBayis; Metzudas Dovid; Binyan HaAsid 682
rows.status: certain (existence/size); 11 amot = Tzuras HaBayis reasoning adopted

rows.claim: Doors north (and south into Ezras Yisroel); 50 amot of open space north of them; same 100 x 50 footprint and storeys as the upper chambers but without atikim; height unknown - author draws 45 amot (upper chambers with atikim ~50)
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:11 + Rashi; Metzudas Dovid; Mishkenei Elyon 187, 197

rows.claim: Upper chambers with atikim also south of the House (20 amot away) and lower chambers also in the SE; on weekdays the people enter the inner court FROM the lower chambers (which have a door into Ezras Yisroel) since the inner east gate is closed except Shabbos/Rosh Chodesh (46:1); the Levites' duchan (stone, 'geder haginah') stands east of the altar between Ezras Yisroel and Ezras Kohanim on a 1-amah step with three half-amah steps (1.5 amot high), facing east; Levites sing there at the wine libation of the tamid morning and evening
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:12 + Rashi; Divrei HaYamim II 5:12; Middos 2:6; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 6:3-5; Mishkenei Elyon 184, 198 ch.2 m.1; Rosh Middos 2:6
rows.status: certain (Rashi/Mishkenei Elyon); passage-through-lower-chambers = author's reading of 42:12
affects: duchan (scene has 4 rises = 1 amah; book 1 + 1.5 = 2.5 amot)

rows.claim: Author's proposals for Second-Temple chambers not named by the navi: Great Sanhedrin (71) on the 3rd floor of the north lower chambers, east end, with a door to chol (outer court) and the lots (payasos) half in kodesh with a door to the inner court; the two courts of 23 at the Har HaBayis east gate (by the Cheil) and in the south lower chambers 2nd floor east; judges sit in a semicircle
rows.source: Sanhedrin 86b; Yoma 25a; Rambam Sanhedrin 1:3; Middos 5:4; author (*)

rows.topic: Where menachos and breads are prepared
rows.claim: Baking of communal menachos, lechem hapanim and shtei halechem in the north 20-amot strip (kodesh); kneading/arranging in the north upper chambers ground floor west (author) or one of the six wall-Ulamim; minchas chinuch and minchas kohen in the south Ulam of the east inner gate (2nd floor); individual menachos of Israelites in the north Ulam of the east gate (3 storeys) since Israelites do not enter the strip
rows.source: Menachos 95b-96a; Rambam Temidin uMusafin 5:7, Maaseh HaKorbanos 12-13; author (*)

rows.claim: Six inspected lambs for the tamid kept 4 days; author places them in the cells of the north inner gate near the slaughter tables (and other communal animals there)
rows.source: Middos 1:6; Arachin 13a; Rambam Temidin uMusafin 1:9; author (*)

rows.topic: Beis HaMoked, mikvaot, Kohen Gadol chamber
rows.claim: Author places in the NORTH LOWER chambers: Lishkas HaChosamos (seals) 1st floor east; Beis HaMoked (domed, stone benches, fire, kohanim sleep) 2nd floor; kohanim's daily mikveh with heating 2nd floor next to it; Kohen Gadol's chamber (Palhedrin, used all year) 2nd floor with his own mikveh; Kohen Gadol's Yom Kippur mikveh in kodesh on the 3rd floor of the west south wall-Ulam (above 'Beis HaParvah'); his house adjacent to Har HaBayis (45:1-9)
rows.source: Tamid 1:1-2; Middos 1:6-9, 5:3-4; Yoma 2a, 19a, 30a; Rambam Klei HaMikdash 5:7, 8:10, Avodas YK 1:3, 2:2-3; author (*)

rows.claim: Incense must be compounded in kodesh; author places it in the south wall-Ulam's west recess, 2nd-3rd floors (with salt chamber and rinsing chamber nearby)
rows.source: Kerisos 6a; Rambam Klei HaMikdash 2:6; Yerushalmi Yoma 1:5; author (*)

rows.topic: Chavitin, clothing, song, oil and wine
rows.claim: Chavitin (Kohen Gadol's daily minchah) prepared in the south Ulam of the east inner gate; clothing chamber north of the east gate (40:46); Levites' song chamber divided in two at the east shoulder of the north gate (40:44-45); oil and wine stores in the south lower chambers 2nd floor with a small daily stock in a south wall-Ulam
rows.source: Middos 1:4, 2:5-6; Yechezkel 40:44-46; author (*)
rows.status: positions of song/clothing chambers certain; stores = author
affects: inner court chambers (scene 'Song chamber' is in the SW, book: NE of the north gate)

rows.claim: Wood store: north lower chambers 2nd floor east, small stock in a north wall-Ulam (long logs for the main pyre, short for the incense pyre, amah-square cut pieces); nazirites' chamber: south lower chambers east 1st floor (not in the four corner courts, which cook only kodashim kalim in the Third Temple); metzoraim chamber with mikveh: north lower chambers west 1st floor near the inner court entrance; salt chamber: south wall-Ulam west 1st floor; parvah (hide salting): south wall-Ulam east 1st-2nd floors
rows.source: Middos 2:5, 5:3; Nazir 45a; Rambam Nazir 8:3; author (*)

rows.claim: Chamber of the 93 service vessels: NW wall-Ulam, all 3 storeys (author); list of altar/incense/menorah/shulchan vessels (fire pans, rakes, forks, golden cup, basins, gold flask 3 log, gold jug, silver trumpets, measures, Yom Kippur lot box, gold basket 2.5 kav, brush, spoons, oil jugs, tongs...); water for the Azarah (Lishkas HaGolah wheel/cistern) and seating/passage for pilgrims on the 1st floor of the lower chambers
rows.source: Tamid 1:4, 3:4, 5:5; Middos 5:4; Sukkah 48a; Rambam Temidin 6:1; author (*)

rows.claim: Knives on both sides of the Ulam (Rashi 41:12, Radak, Metzudos, Tosafos Yom Tov, Mishkenei Elyon 165, 176): author - north side knives ready for slaughter, south side knives for repair and genizah, racked by 24 mishmaros (diagram 12:45)

rows.claim: Women may sit in the 30 gallery chambers of the outer court (author, after the Second Temple gezuztra); kodshei kodashim slaughtered in the north of the inner court and additionally at the north inner gate (Ulam + between cells) sanctified as inner court; rinsing chamber = slaughterhouse at the west shoulder of the north gate
rows.source: Middos 2:5, 3:5, 5:3; Yechezkel 40:39-43; author (*)

rows.claim: Third Temple inner court has only three gates: north = Shaar HaKorban (kodshei kodashim), south = Shaar HaMayim (water will flow from the KhK to the south gate, 47:1-2) and possibly Shaar HaBechoros; plus the passage from the lower chambers; Second Temple's 7 (or 13) gates are not reproduced
rows.source: Middos 1:4, 2:6; Yechezkel 47:1-2; author
affects: river source at the south gate

rows.source: Yechezkel 42:13; Mishkenei Elyon 186-187, 198; Zevachim 56a; Rambam Beis HaBechirah 6:8

rows.claim: Kohanim eat kodshei kodashim in their four service garments (turban, sash, breeches, checkered tunic; Kohen Gadol 8 gold garments, 4 white on Yom Kippur), then leave the garments in the upper chambers and put on ordinary clothes before going out to the people in the outer court (people's clothes are midras-impure relative to kodesh); no sitting in the Azarah except kings of David - author: kohanim probably eat standing at HIGH tables in the inner court (doubt), may sit in the chambers; the Kohen Gadol (the 'nasi') alone sits to eat in the south pishpash gate beside the Heikhal (44:3)
rows.source: Yechezkel 42:14, 44:3 + Rashi; Chagigah 2:7; Yoma 68b-69b; Zevachim 15b-16a, 23b; Rambam Klei HaMikdash 10:4-5, Bias HaMikdash 5:16-17; Mishkenei Elyon 182

rows.topic: Three camps and who enters where
rows.claim: Third Temple mapping: Machaneh Yisroel = all Yerushalayim up to Har HaBayis (incl. kohanim's and Levites' dwellings around Har HaBayis); Machaneh Leviyah = Har HaBayis gate to the Ulamim of the three inner gates (incl. outer court, the 11 amot behind the House, lower chambers); Machaneh Shechinah = inner gate Ulamim inward (incl. House and upper chambers); non-Jews and corpse-impure stop at the Cheil, tevul yom at the outer court; more stringency in the future (halacha like Beis Shammai)
rows.source: Rambam Beis HaBechirah 7:11-22; Keilim 1:6-9; Chagigah 26a
